items.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 27 at 12:33PM EST until November 27 at 8:00PM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
items.areaDesc: Mercer; Gloucester; Camden; Northwestern Burlington; Delaware; Philadelphia; Lower Bucks
items.description:
* WHAT...One to two feet of inundation above ground level in low-
lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...In New Jersey, Mercer, Gloucester, Camden and
Northwestern Burlington. In Pennsylvania, Delaware,
Philadelphia and Lower Bucks.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM EST this evening.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs
along tidal waterways. Some roads become impassable. Minor
damage to vulnerable structures may begin to occur.
items.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

items.headline: Flood Warning issued November 27 at 8:56AM EST until November 27 at 6:00PM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by rain and backwater effects is expected
along the Manasquan and Metedeconk Rivers.

* WHERE...South Central Monmouth County in central New Jersey...
Northeastern Ocean County in southern New Jersey...

* WHEN...Until 600 PM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas near the Manasquan and
Metedeconk rivers is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 851 AM EST, gauge reports indicated both the Manasquan and
Metedeconk Rivers continued to rise after heavy rain yesterday
and further exacerbated by continued backwater effects from the
tidal flooding today. Flooding is already occurring in the warned
area.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Lakewood, Howell, Ramtown, Allenwood, Point Pleasant and Brielle.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
items.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

items.headline: Flood Warning issued November 27 at 10:50AM EST until November 30 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Boston/Norton MA
items.description:
...The National Weather Service in Norton has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Massachusetts...

Taunton River Near Bridgewater affecting Bristol and Plymouth
Counties.

For the Taunton River...including Bridgewater...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Taunton River near Bridgewater.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Backwater flooding from the Taunton River
will cause flooding of lower Purchade Brook in Middleboro.  This
will cause Woloski Park to become impassable by most vehicles.
Beware of the dangers of crossing flooded roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 AM EST Friday the stage was 7.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage just
after midnight tonight to a crest of 8.5 feet early tomorrow
afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage Sunday evening.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
items.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 100 AM EST.

items.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 26 at 12:54PM EST until November 27 at 3:00PM EST by NWS Boston/Norton MA
items.areaDesc: Eastern Essex; Southeast Middlesex; Suffolk; Eastern Norfolk; Eastern Plymouth; Barnstable; Dukes; Nantucket
items.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways (3.1 to 12.9 feet Mean Lower Low Water).

* WHERE...Eastern Essex MA, Southeast Middlesex MA, Suffolk MA,
Eastern Norfolk MA, Eastern Plymouth MA, Barnstable MA, Dukes
MA and Nantucket MA Counties.

* WHEN...From 8 AM to 3 PM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Shallow pockets of flooding less than one foot deep
affects the lowest lying areas along the coast, including
Morrissey Boulevard in Boston. Most roads remain passable.
Flooding up to one foot deep affects coastal roads on the
North Shore from Salem to Gloucester and Newburyport. Rough
surf will cause flooding on some coastal roads around the time
of high tide due to splashover. Roads remain passable. Low
lying areas and roads near Nantucket Harbor, including Easy
Street, may experience pockets of shallow flooding less than
one foot deep.
items.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

items.areaDesc: Southern Fairfield; Southern New Haven; Southern Westchester; Bronx; Northwest Suffolk; Southwest Suffolk; Northern Queens; Northern Nassau; Southern Nassau
items.description:

expected in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline.

* WHERE...In Connecticut, Southern Fairfield and Southern New
Haven Counties. In New York, Southern Westchester, Bronx,
Northwest Suffolk, Southwest Suffolk, Northern Queens,
Northern Nassau and Southern Nassau Counties.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM EST this afternoon.

* COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Minor flooding in the more vulnerable locations
near the waterfront and shoreline. Some roads and low lying properties
including parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and businesses with
basements near the waterfront will experience minor flooding.

* SHORELINE IMPACTS...For southern Nassau and southwest Suffolk, Breaking
waves of 8 to 10 ft will result in beach flooding and dune erosion during
this morning's high tide. Surf height will gradually lower through the day.
